name: Historic Centre of Mexico City and Xochimilco
description: Mexico City's historic core was laid out by the Spanish in the 16th century directly over the ruins of Tenochtitlan, the Aztec capital. It centres on the vast Zócalo plaza, which can hold nearly 100,000 people, and the continent's largest cathedral. Further south, Xochimilco's canals and artificial islands still reflect the Aztec ingenuity of building a living landscape on water.
